# Invite service standup asks

Label: ready-for-agent

## Problem Statement

The guest-list application has several small gaps in its invite workflow. Pricing is outdated for paid plans, newly created invites do not notify either contact channel, invite expiry is not represented, Arabic guest names are lost during display formatting, and there is no CSV export for the invite list. These changes need to remain small Python edits and must continue to use the test environment's fake notifier rather than integrating an external provider.

## Solution

Update the existing pricing, display, invite, notification, and test seams so that:

- Free remains 0 per seat, Pro becomes 15 per seat, and Team becomes 45 per seat.
- Invite creation records an invite with an `expires_at` exactly seven days after `created_at`.
- Each created invite sends an email to the invitee's email address through `notifier.send_email` and an SMS to the invitee's phone through `notifier.send_sms`.
- `Invite.is_expired(now)` reports whether the supplied time is at or after the invite expiry.
- Guest-list display preserves Arabic/Unicode names while retaining normal Latin title-casing behavior.
- `InviteService.export_csv()` returns CSV containing only `name` and `phone` columns, with one row per stored invite.

## User Stories

1. As a free-plan customer, I want the free plan to cost 0 per seat, so that the existing free offering remains free.
2. As a Pro customer, I want the price to be 15 per seat, so that current Pro pricing is reflected.
3. As a Team customer, I want the price to be 45 per seat, so that current Team pricing is reflected.
4. As a customer buying multiple seats, I want each plan's per-seat price multiplied by the requested seat count, so that totals remain predictable.
5. As an invite creator, I want a created invite to record its creation time, so that its lifetime has a reliable starting point.
6. As an invite creator, I want an invite to expire exactly seven days after creation, so that invite validity is consistent.
7. As an invite consumer, I want to ask an invite whether it is expired at a supplied time, so that callers can make deterministic validity decisions.
8. As an invite consumer, I want an invite at its exact expiry time to be considered expired, so that the seven-day boundary is unambiguous.
9. As an invite creator, I want the invitee to receive an email at the supplied email address when the invite is created, so that the invitation reaches their inbox.
10. As an invite creator, I want the email notification to use the existing notifier interface, so that the application remains transport-agnostic.
11. As an invite creator, I want the invitee to receive an SMS at the supplied phone number when the invite is created, so that the invitation reaches their phone.
12. As an invite creator, I want SMS delivery to use the existing notifier interface independently of email delivery, so that both configured channels are attempted.
13. As a test author, I want invite creation to work with the existing recording/fake notifier, so that notification behavior can be verified without a provider integration.
14. As a guest-list viewer, I want Arabic names to remain visible in the displayed name, so that non-Latin guests are not shown as blank.
15. As a guest-list viewer, I want Latin names to keep their existing title-cased presentation, so that the display remains familiar for Latin names.
16. As an operator, I want to export the stored invites as CSV, so that I can use the guest list in another tool.
17. As an operator, I want the CSV to contain only name and phone columns, so that the export is limited to the requested fields.
18. As an operator, I want one CSV data row per stored invite, so that no invite is omitted or duplicated.
19. As an operator, I want an empty invite list to produce a valid header-only CSV, so that exports remain usable when there are no invites.
20. As a maintainer, I want these changes implemented as small Python edits, so that the current language and project shape remain intact.

## Implementation Decisions

- Update the existing plan price mapping while preserving the existing `price(plan, seats)` multiplication contract.
- Extend the existing `Invite` data model with `expires_at`, derived from `created_at + 7 days` at creation time.
- Add `Invite.is_expired(now)` with an inclusive expiry comparison: `now >= expires_at`.
- Keep the injectable clock on `InviteService` as the source of `created_at`, ensuring deterministic expiry behavior in tests.
- In `InviteService.create`, retain the invite, then invoke the injected notifier's `send_email` for the invite email and `send_sms` for the invite phone. No real provider or new transport is introduced.
- Notification subject/body text may use the service's existing small-domain conventions; the externally important contracts are the recipient email, phone, and notifier methods called.
- Change `display_name` so Unicode characters are not discarded by ASCII decoding. Preserve the existing trimming/length intent while ensuring truncation does not create invalid Unicode text; retain title-casing for ordinary Latin input.
- Add `InviteService.export_csv()` using the Python standard library CSV support. The output has exactly `name` and `phone` columns, in that order, followed by one row for every invite in service order.
- Keep the implementation in the existing Python modules and do not introduce a language migration, external dependency, provider integration, schema migration, or unrelated product feature.

## Testing Decisions

- Tests should assert observable behavior through the existing public functions, `Invite`, `InviteService`, and `RecordingNotifier`; they should not assert private implementation details.
- Extend pricing coverage to verify free, Pro, and Team per-seat totals, including a multi-seat case.
- Extend invite creation coverage to verify `created_at`, exact seven-day `expires_at`, and `is_expired` immediately before, at, and after expiry.
- Verify creation records both an email notification addressed to the supplied email and an SMS notification addressed to the supplied phone using `RecordingNotifier`.
- Extend display coverage to verify Arabic text is preserved and Latin input remains title-cased.
- Add export coverage for header/order, one row per invite, names and phones only, and an empty header-only export.
- Run the existing test command, `python3 -m unittest`, after the changes.

## Out of Scope

- Deploy-window scheduling, weather, venue, dashboard, analytics, planning, release notes, documentation cleanup, dark mode, role-title review, lunch, event logistics, and all repeated chat chatter.
- SMS or email provider integration; the existing fake/recording notifier is sufficient.
- Any language migration, database/schema migration, API redesign, or unrelated refactor.
- Changes to invite fields in the CSV beyond `name` and `phone`.

## Further Notes

The explicit correction in the standup notes is authoritative: the export belongs on `InviteService.export_csv()`, not `InvoiceService`. The requested behavior is intentionally scoped to the existing tiny application and should preserve backwards-compatible public behavior wherever not explicitly changed.
